original_question: For the Wang-Swendsen-Kotecky (WSK) dynamics for zero-temperature Potts colorings on periodic lattices, for which lattice sizes n is the dynamics ergodic in the currently unresolved cases q=4 on an n x n periodic triangular lattice and q=3 on an n x n Kagome lattice?
target_in_paper: The paper’s open-problem target is the zero-temperature ergodicity question for Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký dynamics on the q-coloring model on non-bipartite periodic lattices, with the 4-state triangular-lattice case singled out as the key unresolved toroidal case; via the standard zero-temperature correspondence, this is the same finite-size Kempe-connectivity/ergodicity problem for the 3-state kagomé lattice.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the WSK dynamics, the zero-temperature/proper-coloring regime, the two relevant non-bipartite lattices (triangular and kagomé), and the two color numbers q=4 and q=3 that are paired by the paper’s surrounding literature. It also correctly aims at a finite-size classification problem rather than an infinite-volume phase-transition question.
missing_details: The phrase "currently unresolved" is not paper-stable. For paper-faithfulness it should be anchored to Sokal’s 2000 survey/open-problem setting, not to March 25, 2026.
The boundary condition should be stated explicitly as fully periodic boundary conditions, i.e. a finite lattice embedded on a torus.

The paper-faithful finite-volume objects are toroidal periodic triangular-lattice graphs (and the corresponding kagomé graphs), not necessarily only square n x n tori; restricting to n x n may be narrower than the paper’s intended scope.
Ergodicity should be defined as irreducibility of the zero-temperature WSK Markov chain on the finite set of proper q-colorings.
An equivalent graph-theoretic formulation should be made explicit: zero-temperature WSK ergodicity is the same as saying that all proper q-colorings lie in a single Kempe-equivalence class.

The triangular q=4 and kagomé q=3 cases are not two unrelated problems; the zero-temperature 4-state triangular model is essentially equivalent to the 3-state kagomé model, so the question should say this if both are mentioned.
The problem is about finite torus sizes, not about free boundary conditions or general surfaces.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the missing mathematical data are instead the graph family, the boundary conditions, the state space, and the precise meaning of ergodicity.
refined_question: In the sense of Sokal’s 2000 open problem, classify the finite fully periodic triangular-lattice tori (equivalently, via the zero-temperature 4-state triangular/3-state kagomé correspondence, the corresponding fully periodic kagomé lattices) for which the zero-temperature Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký dynamics is ergodic; that is, determine for which torus sizes the proper 4-colorings of the triangular lattice, equivalently the proper 3-colorings of the kagomé lattice, form a single Kempe-equivalence class.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: for the relevant finite toroidal lattices, determine exactly when every pair of proper zero-temperature colorings is connected by a sequence of Kempe changes, since zero-temperature WSK moves are precisely Kempe moves on proper colorings.
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper’s dynamics/ergodicity side rather than its equilibrium or complex-zero problems. The target problem is not a general Potts-model question but the finite-volume zero-temperature ergodicity of WSK on periodic non-bipartite lattices. The closest paper-faithful sharpening is therefore a toroidal-size classification question for WSK/Kempe connectivity. Two corrections are needed to make the draft stand alone and faithful. First, the date-sensitive phrase "currently unresolved" must be replaced by a paper-time anchor: in later work, Mohar and Salas explicitly describe the triangular-lattice torus problem as an open question arising from Sokal’s survey, and they later solve large families of torus sizes; by 2026 these cases are no longer simply "currently unresolved." Second, the triangular q=4 and kagomé q=3 cases should be tied together explicitly rather than listed as separate unrelated problems, because the triangular 4-state zero-temperature model is essentially equivalent to the kagomé 3-state zero-temperature model. The refined wording also makes explicit the hidden definitions that ergodicity is irreducibility of the zero-temperature WSK chain and is equivalent to Kempe connectivity of proper colorings.
